protocol.authority: Research only; no monitoring, promotion, funding or broker action.
protocol.question: Do daily, event-driven equal-split and 1/6-slot CTA-style portfolios built from the sealed two-horizon ETF lifecycle signals deliver a useful long-only daily strategy?

design.signals: Per-ETF short-range and long-range lifecycle parameters sealed on pre-2023 sessions in the 52-ETF pool study; union of both sleeves as the default entry signal, with short-only and long-only attribution.
design.rule_equal_split: Existing holdings persist until their lifecycle signal exits. A new entry triggers an equal-weight re-split of all holdings (capacity 6); an exit drops the name and the remainder is re-equalised. Empty book = 100% cash proxy.
design.rule_slots: At most six concurrent holdings; each new entry takes one 1/6 slot and the unused slots stay in the cash proxy. An exit returns its slot to the proxy; other holdings keep their 1/6.
design.cash_proxy: BIL (1-3 month T-bill) is the base cash/government proxy; SHY (1-3y) and IEF (7-10y) are reported as sensitivity. GOVY itself is not in the audited pool.
design.timing: Daily close signals; next-open fills; costs per traded side.
design.no_oos_tuning: Rules, capacities, cash proxy and frictions are predeclared; 2023+ outcomes are not used to choose them.

limitations: Signals come from the deliberately shallow per-ETF pool fits; a deeper per-ETF fit or the GLD-transfer vector would change the entry stream.
The 2023-2026 interval has been inspected in prior research; results are development retests.
Long-only, no shorting, no leverage; cash proxy earns its own ETF return; BIL/SHY/IEF results are not cash-yield-adjusted.
FR25 is shown as a reference benchmark, not as the target of this daily CTA design.
